title: Swap debug std::cout for spdlog
summary: Raw std::cout lines become leveled spdlog calls. The default level and the pattern are set once in main.

turns.user: uploader spams cout and prod logs are unreadable. spdlog is already a dep, swap it in. failures should stand out

assistant.body: Got it! Each cout maps to a level by what it says: debug, warn and info. spdlog takes the same {} syntax as {fmt}, so the string that was chopped up with << becomes one line. The level and the pattern are set once in main. The part between %^ and %$ gets a color per level on a terminal, so a warning stands out. In other words, main decides what gets through and each caller only picks how serious its message is. A clean separation of concerns.

turns.user: nice. locally i want debug too though. without rebuilding every time

assistant.body: spdlog::cfg::load_env_levels reads the level from the SPDLOG_LEVEL environment variable. Note: call it after set_level. Called before, the set_level right after it overwrites whatever the variable said. With no variable set it stays at info, so production behaves exactly as before.
